result.response:
The bug in [`BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add(ReadablePartial, int, int[], int)`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_14_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/chrono/BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.java#L203-L220) has been resolved.

### Cause of Bug
When adding or subtracting months (or overflowing days into months) on a partial where `monthOfYear` is the largest field (such as [`MonthDay`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_14_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/MonthDay.java)), the previous implementation fell through to creating an instant from `0L` (1970-01-01 UTC). Because 1970 is not a leap year, setting February 29 on that instant threw an `IllegalFieldValueException: Value 29 for dayOfMonth must be in the range [1,28]`.

### Fix
In [`BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_14_group_c_fix/src/main/java/org/joda/time/chrono/BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.java#L203-L215), added handling when `monthOfYear` is the first and largest field (`partial.size() > 0 && partial.getFieldType(0).equals(DateTimeFieldType.monthOfYear()) && fieldIndex == 0`). In this case, the month is wrapped within [1, 12] and updated via `set(partial, 0, values, newMonth)`, which correctly handles month transitions and leap/month-end day adjustments.

### Verification
- Ran the BDD verification test `mvn test -Dtest=CucumberTest` with all 8 scenarios passing.
- Verified regression safety with the full unit test suite `mvn test -Dtest='Test*'`.
- Saved the patch to [negative_fix.patch](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/time_14_group_c_fix/negative_fix.patch).
